h1: Tawa Ravadee Resort Prachinburi — a 4-star garden resort by a lake in Thailand's herbal-medicine province
intro: If you want somewhere in Prachinburi that's a genuine garden resort rather than an in-town tower — lotus ponds, wide lawns, a big pool, and rooms whose balconies open onto a lake — Tawa Ravadee Resort is the name that comes up most in the province. It's a 4-star, 199-room WorldHotels Distinctive property in Si Maha Phot District. Rooms run 38 sqm with private balconies looking over the garden or lake, and rates start at about ฿1,900/night. It suits self-drivers on a getaway, conference groups, or anyone stopping by on the way to Chao Phraya Abhaibhubejhr Hospital.

body.html: What sets Tawa Ravadee apart from other places to stay in Prachinburi is that it's a full garden resort. The grounds are laid out as tropical gardens with lotus ponds, wide lawns, shaded walkways and low-rise room blocks spread around. From the tree-lined entrance drive to the tall, airy lobby, guests often say it feels like slipping out of town into a quiet garden — even though it's only about ninety minutes from Bangkok.

All 199 rooms are around 38 sqm, and every one comes with a 6 sqm private balcony opening onto a garden or lake view. They're done in contemporary Thai style with silk fabrics and wooden furniture, and the bathrooms have both a tub and a hot-water shower. Reviews consistently praise the spacious rooms, comfy beds, and the balcony views that make you want to linger over morning coffee. The hotel had a major renovation in 2024, so the updated rooms feel fresher than the older stock.
"Really spacious room, opened the balcony to a view over the lake, woke up to have coffee and birdsong, and the pool is big and genuinely lovely — great value for a small town like this."

Facilities are generous for an upcountry resort. There's a large outdoor swimming pool, a fitness room, a sauna, tennis courts, a massage room and the Thiwa Ratree restaurant. Breakfast is another thing reviews mention often — a buffet with both Thai and European dishes, decent coffee, and a fair spread of fresh items. The wide grounds suit families wanting space for kids to run around, and conference groups who want meeting rooms and accommodation in one place.

The resort is in Si Maha Phot District on Highway 3079, about 20 minutes' drive from central Prachinburi and Chao Phraya Abhaibhubejhr Hospital. It's roughly 140 km from Suvarnabhumi Airport, or 1.5 hours by car. The big plus is the quiet, since it sits well off the main road — but the trade-off is that you really need a car, as there are no shops or restaurants within walking distance.

To be straight about it, there are a few things reviews flag. The most common are slow Wi-Fi in some rooms and dated TVs. Some guests find hot water that isn't consistently strong, and check-in/check-out can be slow when groups arrive together. One more thing to set expectations: the resort is in an area not far from an industrial zone, and a small number of reviews mention an odd smell on some nights when the wind blows that way — not everyone runs into it, but it's worth knowing.

Overall, Tawa Ravadee Resort scores 8.7 out of 10 on Trip.com from around 94 real reviews, and 4.1 out of 5 on Tripadvisor from 123 reviews. It's a strong fit for self-drivers who want wide garden grounds, a room with a lake-view balcony, a big pool and good breakfast at the low-thousands price point. Rates start around ฿1,900 and rise with the season and room type up to the lake-view suites. If you can live with needing a car and a few aging details around the property, it's the best pick in Prachinburi.

honestSummary: Tawa Ravadee Resort is the best garden resort in Prachinburi for self-drivers who want wide grounds, a room with a lake-view balcony and a big pool at the low-thousands price point — lovely gardens, good breakfast, and more facilities than the in-town hotels. The trade-offs are the location that needs a car and a few aging details around the buildings.
honestChecks: If you don't have a car — the resort is out of town with nothing walkable nearby → if you'd rather stay in the city with food within walking distance, consider IRabbit Hotel or Jiphome in town instead.
If you're particular about Wi-Fi and room freshness — some rooms have slow internet and dated TVs → ask for a room renovated in 2024 and keep mobile data as a backup.

If you're sensitive to smells — a small number of reviews mention an odd smell from the industrial area on some nights → choose a lake-side room and ask reception about the wind direction before you check in.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Tawa Ravadee Resort Prachinburi

faq.q: Where is Tawa Ravadee Resort in Prachinburi, and what's nearby?
faq.a: Tawa Ravadee Resort is at 77 Moo 7, Tha Tum, Si Maha Phot District, Prachinburi, on Highway 3079. It's about 20 minutes' drive from central Prachinburi and Chao Phraya Abhaibhubejhr Hospital, near Si Mahosot Ancient City, and roughly 140 km (1.5 hours) from Suvarnabhumi Airport.

faq.q: How much does Tawa Ravadee Resort cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start at around ฿1,900/night for a garden-view Superior Room. Choices run from Superior and lake-view Deluxe up to Duplex and Lake View Suite. All rooms are 38 sqm with a private balcony. Prices rise with the season and room type — always compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Does Tawa Ravadee Resort have a pool and what facilities are there?
faq.a: Yes, and they're fairly complete. There's a large outdoor swimming pool, a fitness room, a sauna, tennis courts, a massage room and the Thiwa Ratree restaurant, all set among tropical gardens and lotus ponds. It suits families and conference groups, and the Thai/European breakfast buffet is a frequent review highlight.

faq.q: What are the rooms like at Tawa Ravadee Resort?
faq.a: Rooms are 38 sqm in contemporary Thai style with silk fabrics and wooden furniture. Every room has a private balcony with a garden or lake view and a bathtub in the bathroom. The hotel was renovated in 2024, but some rooms still have slow Wi-Fi or dated TVs, so ask for a recently renovated room.

faq.q: Who is Tawa Ravadee Resort best for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for self-drivers on a garden-resort getaway, families and conference groups who want wide grounds, a lake-view balcony and a big pool. Because it's out of town with nothing walkable nearby, it's less suited to anyone without a car or who wants to stay in the city centre.

faq.q: Is there a smell from factories at Tawa Ravadee Resort?
faq.a: Most guests don't run into it, but a small number of reviews mention an odd smell from the industrial area on some nights when the wind blows that way. It's not everyone and not every night. If you're concerned, choose a lake-side room and ask reception about the wind direction before you check in.
